name: Question 18
problem: A particle $P$ of mass $6\,kg$ moves along the $x$-axis under the action of a force of magnitude $(8-x)\,N$ acting in the direction of increasing $x.$ Given that $x$ is measured in meters, and the particle has velocity $v=6\,m/s$ at $x=1,$ calculate the velocity of the particle at $x=3.$
worked_solution:
The work-energy principle states that the work done by a resultant force on a particle equals the change in the particle's kinetic energy. That is,

$$
W=Δ\,\text{KE}
$$

where the change in kinetic energy of a particle is given by

$$
Δ\,\text{KE}=\frac{1}{2}m{v}_{1}^{2}-\frac{1}{2}m{v}_{0}^{2}
$$

and $m$ is the particle's mass, ${v}_{0}$ is its initial velocity, and ${v}_{1}$ is its final velocity.

First, we calculate the work done by the force in moving the particle from $x=1$ to $x=3:$

$$
\begin{aligned}W & ={\int }_{{x}_{1}}^{{x}_{2}}F(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}(8-x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[8x-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}]}_{1}^{3} \\  & =(24-\frac{9}{2})-(8-\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =12\,J\end{aligned}
$$

The particle has velocity $v=6\,m/s$ at $x=1.$ So, we can find the velocity ${v}_{1}$ at $x=3$ using the work-energy principle:

$$
\begin{aligned}W & =\frac{1}{2}m{v}_{1}^{2}-\frac{1}{2}m{v}_{0}^{2} \\ 12 & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 6\cdot {v}_{1}^{2}-\frac{1}{2}\cdot 6\cdot {6}^{2} \\ 12 & =3{v}_{1}^{2}-108 \\ 3{v}_{1} & =120 \\ {v}_{1}^{2} & =40 \\ {v}_{1} & =\pm \sqrt{40} \\ {v}_{1} & =\pm 2\sqrt{10}.\end{aligned}
$$

We can disregard the negative solution since the velocity and acceleration of the particle are positive in the regions under consideration. 

Therefore, the velocity of the particle at $x=3$ is $2\sqrt{10}\,m/s.$

Question 18
?

A particle P of mass 6kg moves along the x-axis under the action of a force of magnitude (8−x)N acting in the direction of increasing x. Given that x is measured in meters, and the particle has velocity v=6m/s at x=1, calculate the velocity of the particle at x=3.

a
210m/s
b
5m/s
c
25m/s
d
10m/s
e
22m/s
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The work-energy principle states that the work done by a resultant force on a particle equals the change in the particle's kinetic energy. That is,

W=ΔKE

where the change in kinetic energy of a particle is given by

ΔKE=12mv12−12mv02

and m is the particle's mass, v0 is its initial velocity, and v1 is its final velocity.

First, we calculate the work done by the force in moving the particle from x=1 to x=3:

W=∫x1x2F(x)dx=∫13(8−x)dx=[8x−x22]13=(24−92)−(8−12)=12J

The particle has velocity v=6m/s at x=1. So, we can find the velocity v1 at x=3 using the work-energy principle:

W=12mv12−12mv0212=12⋅6⋅v12−12⋅6⋅6212=3v12−1083v1=120v12=40v1=±40v1=±210.

We can disregard the negative solution since the velocity and acceleration of the particle are positive in the regions under consideration.

Therefore, the velocity of the particle at x=3 is 210m/s.
